T15.reason: the sweep and architecture search run many training jobs: the cost is the number of trials

T16.reason: the Noether trainer needs a symmetry declaration and the residual it is applied to

T17.reason: the advisor and the audit read a finished run's history; there is no one call to time

T18.reason: MAML / Reptile are an inner loop per task: the cost is tasks x inner steps

T19.reason: transfer learning needs a source checkpoint and a target data set

T2.reason: DDP / FSDP / SLURM / torchrun: the cost is the number of ranks the job is launched with, not one process's call

T20.reason: the self-scaled quasi-Newton step converges in one or two iterations whatever the parameter count is, so its cost is set by the caller's objective: a quadratic in 64, 256 and 1024 parameters all took 0.19 ms

T21.reason: the autoresearch loop runs a budget of trials: the cost is the budget

T22.probe: pinneapple_neural.lpm.FourierEncoding.__call__ (the large-physics-model positional encoding over a point cloud)

T23.reason: MultiAdam keeps per-term moments inside the training step, so its cost is a fraction of the backward pass T1 measures

T3.reason: causal training schedules the collocation points of a trainer run; it is a policy inside T1's loop

T4.reason: time marching trains one window per step, so the cost is the number of windows of the case

T5.reason: the two-phase schedule (Adam then L-BFGS) needs a model, a loss and a data set from the caller

T6.reason: multi-restart is the training cost multiplied by the number of restarts

T7.reason: adaptive collocation needs the residual it resamples, i.e. a trainer run to measure

T8.reason: the loss balancers (ReLoBRaLo, SoftAdapt, PCGrad, ...) are scalar or gradient operations inside the training step: their cost is a fraction of the backward pass T1 measures

T9.reason: the weight schedulers (SA-PINN, GradNorm, LossRatio, NTK) run inside the training step, on quantities the backward pass produces
